blocks.title: Phishing Awareness and Response exam shortcuts
items: Company deliberately sends fake phishing emails → PHISHING CAMPAIGN
The goal is awareness training and measurement, not real compromise.
Example: Users who click receive targeted training.
Urgency + strange link + credential request → PHISHING ATTEMPT
Look for multiple social-engineering red flags.
Example: 'Your account expires in 10 minutes—sign in here.'
User reports suspicious email → RESPOND TO THE REPORT
Security should analyze, contain, and communicate as needed.
Example: Block the malicious domain and warn recipients.
blocks.example: First identify the human-security problem: phishing, suspicious behavior, user guidance, or awareness-program measurement.

questions.q: A company deliberately sends fake phishing emails to employees and measures who clicks the links. What is this?
questions.explanation: A phishing campaign is a simulated awareness exercise used to train and measure users.

questions.q: An email creates urgency, asks the user to sign in immediately, and links to a lookalike domain. What should the user recognize?
questions.explanation: Urgency, deceptive links, and credential requests are common phishing indicators.

questions.q: A user reports a suspicious message to the security team. What should happen next?
choices: Analyze the message and take containment actions if needed
Ignore it if no one clicked
questions.explanation: Reported suspicious messages should be analyzed and, if malicious, blocked and communicated appropriately.

questions.q: A simulated phishing exercise shows that one department has a high click rate. What is the best next step?
questions.explanation: Phishing campaigns are used to identify training needs and improve user behavior.
